title: Read every available and permitted CPU, GPU, NVMe, Wi-Fi and ACPI temperature channel on Ubuntu and Windows.
changes: Merge Linux kernel hwmon and thermal-zone inventories instead of stopping at the first ACPI channel. Keep chip and sensor labels, de-duplicate equivalent ACPI readings and distinguish multiple disks with identical labels.

On Linux and Windows, optionally include NVIDIA GPU die temperatures through a fixed, read-only, timeout-bounded nvidia-smi query. Keep sensor and output limits to 64 validated Celsius readings; never synthesize missing measurements.

On Windows, probe available LibreHardwareMonitor/OpenHardwareMonitor WMI temperature providers and firmware-exposed ACPI thermal zones with a fixed, noninteractive PowerShell script. Correctly convert ACPI tenths of Kelvin to Celsius without claiming it measures CPU die temperature.
Preserve the larger hardware inventory through the owner-only diagnostic normalization boundary and System Monitor, rejecting suspicious names, nonnumeric values and out-of-range temperatures.

Verify on ASUS: six simultaneous real hwmon channels instead of one; desktop and 390/320-pixel browser screenshots without horizontal overflow. Add Linux/Windows parsing, failure-mode, source-label and NVIDIA regressions.

Retain the verified Apple Silicon native-addon installation fix from v0.2.200. On Windows, full hardware coverage depends on exposed vendor data; no external driver installation, elevation, or permission changes occur automatically.
